title: Building Applications with AI Agents — Michael Albada, Microsoft
talk_summary: Michael Albada (Microsoft) gives a principles-level talk on production agent systems: tool design, orchestration patterns, evaluation, observability, and pitfalls.

takeaways.technique: Cap and semantically group tools per agent
takeaways.what_they_do: Avoid one-to-one API-to-tool mapping; expose fewer, clearly named tools grouped by semantic similarity, because accuracy degrades as tool count per completion rises.

takeaways.technique: Deterministic business logic outside the model
takeaways.what_they_do: Expose tools that update explicit state with validation/sanitization, and keep fixed business rules in deterministic code rather than asking the LLM to apply them.

takeaways.technique: Eval set as test-driven development for agents
takeaways.what_they_do: Build a labeled input/output eval set from real runs plus human review, then batch-run and cluster failures to choose hyperparameters (model, tool count, memory) instead of developing by anecdote.
takeaways.evidence_quote: invest more in evaluation ... it's moving us towards a type of test-driven development with agents

takeaways.technique: Red-team and synthetic inputs before shipping
takeaways.what_they_do: Use synthetic data generation (Intel Agent) and red-teaming tools (PyRIT) to stress agents before deployment, and add trip-wires/detectors that eject to human review.
takeaways.evidence_quote: make sure that you're building trip wires and detectors at different stages of your aentic stack so that you can eject out and fall back

takeaways.technique: Prefer simple chains/trees over full agency
takeaways.what_they_do: Use single chains and LLM-routed branching where possible; only escalate to full agentic loops when chains become unmaintainable, since chains are easier to measure and cheaper.
takeaways.evidence_quote: If it can fall into a single chain, please do that. It will make it easier to measure. It will keep your cost down.

takeaways.technique: Observability with tracing and failure clustering
takeaways.what_they_do: Instrument agents with OpenTelemetry-style tracing and logs, then cluster/summarize failures to find dominant failure modes rather than reading individual traces.
takeaways.evidence_quote: detailed logs and tracing and probably some way of doing additional clustering and automated summarization to understand those main categories of failure modes
